items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1973-08-06
items.q: He went with me as a bass player.

ctx.x: What about if a guy got sick? And you're on the road.

That's another question. It's hard for me to answer. I don't remember anybody getting sick, but one time was Turner, wasn't it? What about that? Well, that was in later years. But Henry Turner got real sick in a little town of Ashland, Kentucky, I think. It was in the hills. And we had to...no, I'm sorry. Another fellow, Buddy Collins. He was from here. I don't know if you ever hear any talk about him. He was a vocalist. You've told me about him. Yeah. Well, Nick Turner got sick in this little small town in the…
I don't know if he's still going or not. You were going to say something?

items.title: Don Albert and Herbert Hall Interview, 1978-08-03
items.q: We picked up Henry Turner, played two bands I've never seen of him before.

ctx.x: One of him at that time. And he...

It wasn't a very big band there, it was Don Hubbard and his 10 Pals. Well, he put a 10 then. It wasn't even 10 then, we didn't get the 10 until we got to Dallas and picked up Adam Hardy. We picked up Henry Turner, played two bands I've never seen of him before. Oh, well, he was the first one in the band. Yeah, I've never seen a heard of him before in my life.
You didn't have a string bass at that time?

items.title: Don Albert Interview, 1974-01-01
items.q: And of course, Nicky got his name, Nicky.

ctx.x: Well, supposing some of the musicians would be talking about your coat or your tie. They'd say, watch it say the hawk's going to get it. They'd be having a cue to get hold of whatever it was, whoever the hawk was. I imagine somebody knew who the hawk was but they never knew. And then they used to call her, if a chick wasn't a nice looking chick, they would call her Taylor. And then she was not such a nice looking gal. What do you call her? Well, they call her a good looking chick. That's a nice looking Taylor.…
So, I guess, unless you can make something else, we'd better turn it up. We're almost to the end of the tape. Okay, thank you. Goodnight, Nicky. Goodnight.
